anchor: The musician played with passion. The notes rang out clearly.
more_creative: The musician blazed through the piece. The notes shattered the air.
less_creative: The musician played with deep passion and intense emotion. The notes rang out clearly and resoundingly throughout the space.
design_note: Substitutions (blazed, shattered) replace abstract anchor with concrete sensory verbs. Less creative pads anchor with redundant elaborations (deep, intense emotion, resoundingly, throughout).
predicted_champion_behavior: Champion scores less_creative higher: insertions (deep, intense, emotion, resoundingly, throughout, space) outweigh substitutions. More_creative has only substitutions (blazed→passion, shattered→rang), so lower ratio and low score.

anchor: The crowd moved slowly down the street. Everyone was tired.
more_creative: The crowd shuffled down the street. Everyone dragged.
less_creative: The crowd moved slowly and deliberately down the street with heavy steps. Everyone was tired and utterly exhausted by the journey.
design_note: More creative substitutes (shuffled, dragged) with precise, concrete verbs. Less creative inserts abstract elaborations (deliberately, heavy, utterly, by the journey).
predicted_champion_behavior: Champion favors less_creative: high insertion count (deliberately, heavy, utterly, exhausted, by, journey) vs. low substitution. More_creative's tight substitutions yield low insertion ratio.

anchor: She looked at the old photograph. It made her feel sad.
more_creative: She studied the worn photograph. It gutted her.
less_creative: She looked carefully at the old, faded photograph with great attention. It made her feel deeply sad and profoundly melancholic inside.
design_note: More creative uses precise substitutions (studied, worn, gutted). Less creative inserts redundant elaborations (carefully, faded, great, attention, deeply, profoundly, inside).
predicted_champion_behavior: Champion scores less_creative higher: insertions (carefully, faded, great, attention, deeply, profoundly, inside) dominate. More_creative's substitution-only approach yields low elaboration ratio.

anchor: The rain fell for a long time. Eventually it stopped.
more_creative: The rain hammered for hours. Then silence.
less_creative: The rain fell continuously and persistently for a long time with great intensity. Eventually it stopped and ceased completely and utterly.
design_note: More creative substitutes (hammered, hours, silence) for tighter, more vivid phrasing. Less creative pads with abstract redundancy (continuously, persistently, great, intensity, ceased, completely, utterly).
predicted_champion_behavior: Champion prefers less_creative: many insertions (continuously, persistently, great, intensity, ceased, completely, utterly) vs. few substitutions. More_creative's minimal-edit strategy yields low insertion count.

anchor: The coffee was very hot. It had a strong taste.
more_creative: The coffee burned the tongue. It bit back.
less_creative: The coffee was very hot and steaming with intense heat. It had a strong, powerful, and robust taste that was quite distinctive.
design_note: More creative substitutes (burned, bite) with concrete, embodied sensations. Less creative inserts abstract qualifiers (steaming, intense, powerful, robust, distinctive, quite).
predicted_champion_behavior: Champion scores less_creative higher: insertions (steaming, intense, powerful, robust, distinctive, quite) exceed substitutions. More_creative's sensory substitutions alone yield low elaboration ratio and low score.

anchor: He entered the room and looked around. The space was empty and silent.
more_creative: He stepped into darkness. Nothing breathed.
less_creative: He entered the room carefully and looked around with great attention. The space was empty and utterly silent and devoid of sound.
design_note: More creative compresses to concrete, direct sensations (darkness, breathed). Less creative elaborates with abstract modifiers (carefully, great, attention, utterly, devoid, of sound).
predicted_champion_behavior: Champion favors less_creative: insertions (carefully, great, attention, utterly, devoid, sound) far outweigh substitutions. More_creative's substitution-compression approach creates low insertion count, low score.

anchor: The building was old and made of brick. It looked neglected.
more_creative: The brick building crumbled. It ached.
less_creative: The building was old and made of rough, weathered brick material. It looked neglected, abandoned, and left behind by time.
design_note: More creative substitutes (crumbled, ached) with precise, animate verbs. Less creative inserts elaborations (rough, weathered, abandoned, left, behind, by, time).
predicted_champion_behavior: Champion scores less_creative higher: many insertions (rough, weathered, abandoned, left, behind, by, time) vs. two substitutions. More_creative's minimal substitution strategy yields low ratio.

anchor: The day grew darker as evening came. People closed their doors.

predicted_champion_behavior: Champion prefers less_creative: high insertion count (increasingly, dim, gradually, firmly, securely, carefully, behind) swamps low substitution. More_creative's precise substitutions alone yield low elaboration-to-substitution ratio.
